correctness.rationale: Solving D′=aL0e^(−at)−bD before and after an instantaneous multiplication by q gives g(t)=C(e^(−at)−e^(−bt)) and post D_s(t)=C[e^(−at)−A(s)e^(−bt)] for t≥s, A=q+(1−q)e^((b−a)s). The upstream maximum g(s) strictly increases for s<t0; the downstream constrained maximum Q_T(s), at t=min(T,h(s)), strictly decreases with s there because moving the aerator later makes post deficit pointwise lower for t≥later position. Their unique crossing gives global minimax and excludes endpoint/late placements. The unconstrained post peak m(s) decreases, so the unique g(s∞)=m(s∞) defines T_c=h(s∞); for T≥T_c the downstream peak is present and the site stays fixed. Below T_c the balance occurs at the reach endpoint and implicit differentiation gives increasing s_T. Taylor at h(s) where D_s″(h)=−ab m(s), plus J=g′−m′>0, yields the quadratic cutoff law; short reach Taylor yields 1/(2−q). Independent numerical scans over 125 random parameter instances were consistent and exact a=1,b=2,q=.5 matches s∞ and Tc, but scans are not a universal proof.
residual_risks: The argument that a site s∞ can be compared below T_c must be read only when T≥s∞; when T<s∞ the s_T<s∞ conclusion is immediate from feasibility, so this is expository imprecision not a false theorem.
The model treats only one fixed-fraction impulse and constant coefficients.
